source.n8n_access: read-only GET /executions only; reasoned from the node's own contract (lines 32-35 of detect-media.js).
source.rationale: The fail-safe: an audio attachment respond.io has not finished uploading (isPending, no url) MUST NOT enter the media lane, because media-extract-http would post a null media_url and the CRM would refuse - a refusal message the customer sees for a message they sent perfectly well. The body drops modality back to null so the turn falls through to tf-message and the existing pipeline answers on the caption, which is today's behaviour. The invariant this pins is that only `modality` is cleared: `attachment_type` still reads 'audio' and mime_type still reads 'audio/ogg', so the trace stays truthful about what actually arrived.
